correctness.rationale: Derived directly from the one-dimensional sketched harmonic Petrov--Galerkin pencil. On the fixed two-eigenmode plane, the sign for all directions is exactly positive definiteness of a 2-by-2 symmetric Jordan-product matrix; its Sylvester determinant is positive precisely when the squared Gaussian-column cosine is below \(4\kappa/(1+\kappa)^2\). Independent Gaussian directions give the Beta(1/2,(s-1)/2) distribution. A negative determinant yields an explicit negative-Ritz witness. Strict stochastic ordering in s and the spherical-coordinate normal limit prove the exact row-budget constant; the beta density at zero proves fixed-s asymptotics. Edge cases s=2 and \(\kappa=1\) are covered. Exact rational checks and seeded simulations independently agree; they are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Half-plane positivity of sketched harmonic Ritz values is a stated hypothesis in a recent restarted matrix-function convergence analysis. The result determines the exact simultaneous safe probability and the sharp minimal Gaussian row count on the natural smallest nontrivial eigenmode plane; at any fixed sketch size, uniform safety becomes asymptotically unlikely as conditioning grows. It also separates a shared-sketch guarantee from individually fixed-direction probabilities, a consequential distinction for sketches reused over variable starting directions. This is a complete motivated natural invariant and optimal sample-budget classification, not a generic tail estimate, arbitrary finite slice or a mere type check. Limits to one-dimensional extraction are explicitly stated.
